abstract: The Go implementation of a binary min-heap is a canonical example of a balanced search and indexing structure that underpins many compiler back-ends and runtime schedulers. We analyze the asymptotic complexity of push and pop operations, formally prove the strict min-heap invariant, and evaluate empirical latency and throughput on a single-core AMD EPYC 9V74 platform. The mean latency of 982.06 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 1,018,267 ops/s demonstrate that the algorithm meets the performance expectations of modern compiler pipelines. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/go-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261021_190154_the_compiler_was_supposed_to_e}
